title: Structured Output Assertion + Watchdog (draft)
content:
Summary:
This is a personal design scratchpad for a lightweight assertion/watchdog system that sits on top of Redwood’s generation API and enforces structured-output contracts (JSON/CSV/typed-records) and safeties. The goal is to provide an opt-in, low-latency layer that can: 1) validate structured outputs at inference-time, 2) emit enriched telemetry for rollouts and regressions, and 3) optionally trigger automated repair/fallback flows (re-prompt, model variant, or function-call enforcement).

Why we need this:
- More customers are using structured outputs (JSON, RDF-like blobs, table rows) and depend on strict shapes. Small model drift or prompt change causes silent downstream breaks.
- Current approach (post-hoc evals + sampling) is slow and disconnected from runtime; operators want immediate signals and remedial actions.
- Should be lightweight, usable in hosted API and in private deployments with minimal infra changes.

Non-goals:
- Not a full schema language or validator (don’t re-implement JSON Schema). Start with a compact contract format + common checks.
- Not intended to block critical low-latency paths by default — default behavior is observe-only / soft-fail unless customer opts into enforcement.

Core Concepts:
- Assertion Contract: short declarative document attached to a route (or passed with request) describing required fields, types, example constraints, and a small set of predicates (presence, type, enum, numeric range, regex, semantics).
- Watchdog: runtime component that validates the assertion result and emits events + metrics; can execute configured remediations when assertions fail.
- Repair actions: re-prompt with stronger instruction, call deterministic tool (parser/serializer), fall back to a different model variant or return a structured default.

Contract (compact example) - canonical string form (YAML-ish but we'll accept JSON):

{
  "contract_id": "order_line_v1",
  "output_format": "json",
  "top_level_type": "object",
  "fields": [
    {"name": "order_id", "type": "string", "presence": "required", "pattern": "^ORD-[0-9]{6}$"},
    {"name": "items", "type": "array", "presence": "required", "min_items": "1"},
    {"name": "total_amount", "type": "number", "presence": "required", "min": "0"},
    {"name": "currency", "type": "string", "presence": "optional", "enum": ["USD", "EUR", "GBP"]}
  ],
  "predicates": [
    {"expr": "len(items) > 0"},
    {"expr": "total_amount >= sum(item.qty * item.unit_price for item in items) - 0.01"}  
  ],
  "severity": "warning"   /* default severity: warning | enforce */
}

Notes on the contract: predicates are small Python-like expressions that the Watchdog evaluates in a sandbox against the parsed output; we’ll restrict operations to avoid Turing-complete risk. We store a compact contract (<=2KB) per route and support inline contracts in calls for ad-hoc checks.

API surface (runtime side) - sketch:
- Route-level config: in route config (console / infra manifest) add: assertions: [contract_id, ...] + enforcement_mode: soft|enforce|observe-only
- Per-request override: request header X-RDW-Assertion: <inline-contract-or-id>
- Response envelope (augmented): server returns normal generated payload; Watchdog returns a companion metadata block when present:
  {
    "watchdog": {
      "contract_id": "order_line_v1",
      "status": "pass|fail|partial",
      "violations": ["items: missing", "total_amount: mismatch"],
      "remediation": "re-prompted to model-variant:gfl-4x; got repaired",
      "latency_ms": 12
    }
  }

Behavior modes:
- observe-only: validate and emit telemetry/trace spans; do not modify response. Good for initial rollouts.
- soft-fail: validate and, on failure, attach 'violations' and optionally call a deterministic post-processor (parser/serializer) to coerce output; return original text plus metadata.
- enforce: block response if critical assertions fail and execute configured repair action (e.g., re-run with stricter system instruction OR fallback to a model variant). Enforce mode should be used with rate limits and guardrails (see failure modes).

Remediation primitives (sketch):
- re_prompt(reprompt_template, max_retries=1): constructs a short correction prompt and resends to model variant.
- parse_with_schema(parser_id): call an internal parser/cleanup library to coerce text into contract (best-effort).
- fallback_variant(variant_id): route the request to alternative model.
- delegate_to_tool(tool_id): call a deterministic tool (e.g., Wasm JSON rewriter) to fix shape.

Telemetry & signals to emit:
- assertion.evaluations.count (by contract_id, status)
- assertion.violations.topN (which predicates fail most)
- assertion.latency.p50/p95 (validation + repairs)
- assertion.remediation.rate (how often remediation used and success rate)
- assertion.false_positive.rate (tracked via manual labels/feedback)
- traces: attach a span for assertion evaluation and each repair attempt, include model variant used and token deltas.

Pseudocode (very high level):

on_response(response_text, contract):
  parsed = try_parse(response_text, contract.output_format)
  if not parsed:
    emit(metric parse_failure)
    if enforcement==enforce and remediation.includes(parse_with_schema):
      repaired = parse_with_schema(response_text, contract)
      if repaired.valid: return repaired + metadata
    if enforcement==enforce: trigger fallback or return structured error
    else: return original_text + metadata(pass=false)

  violations = evaluate_predicates(parsed, contract)
  if violations.empty: return response + metadata(pass=true)
  else if enforcement==observe-only: emit telemetry; return response + metadata(pass=false, violations)
  else: apply_remedies(violations, config)

apply_remedies:
  for action in config.remediation_order:
    outcome = run(action)
    emit(action.attempt)
    if outcome.satisfies(contract): return outcome + metadata(repaired=true)
  // all remediate attempts failed
  if enforcement==soft-fail: attach violations and return original text
  if enforcement==enforce: return structured error + 503 or fallback variant result

Open questions / design trade-offs:
- Where to run validation? At ingress node (fast path) or at dedicated async workers? Running synchronously increases P50/P95 and needs to be carefully profiled.
- Sandboxing predicate language — use a small WASM runtime or a restricted expression evaluator (e.g., tinyexpr) to avoid arbitrary code.
- Cost accounting: remediation actions can double/triple token costs if they re-run models; we need per-route guardrails and a visible billing signal.
- Backpressure: if lots of failures cause flurries of re-prompts, we may overload models. Remediation should incorporate token/burst budgets and global caps.
- Latency vs correctness: offer per-route toggles. For customer-facing low-latency routes start in observe-only + alerting.

Migration path / rollout plan (draft):
1) Build observation-only server-side validation: store contract IDs on route config; emit metrics + traces.
2) Add per-request inline contract support for SDK experiments.
3) Implement simple remediation actions (parser+re_prompt) behind feature flag; start with low-traffic customers.
4) Provide console UI to view assertion violations and top failing predicates; allow toggling enforcement per-route.
5) Add enforcement mode with throttles and hard caps; require an agreement step in console for billing/latency acceptance.

Operational concerns / throttles: 
- Default remediation budget: 10% of route requests or 1000 repairs/day, whichever is lower. Configurable.
- Global remediation kill-switch and per-customer rate-limiter.
- Alerting: SLO burn if assertion.remediation.success_rate drops <75% over 30m.

Developer ergonomics (SDK):
- JavaScript/Go SDK helper to attach inline contract object or contract id.
- Local CLI validator to validate contract and run a quick simulation against sample model responses.
- Provide example contracts for common patterns (keyed object, flat CSV rows, list-of-records).

Example cURL for inline contract (sketch):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{
    "model": "gfl-3b",
    "prompt": "Extract order info from: <email body>",
    "assertion": {"contract_id":"order_line_v1","severity":"warning"}
  }'

At runtime the response body will include the watchdog block in metadata if the assertion system is enabled for that route or provided inline.

Small experiments to validate approach:
- Run on internal dataset of 2k prompts; measure baseline validation failure rate on current models; iterate on small set of repair templates.
- Try both parse-first and re_prompt-first strategies and compare repair success and cost per successful repair.
- Measure extra p95 latency for 'observe-only' path (should be <15ms) and for a single re-prompt repair (expected +200ms-800ms depending on model).

TODO (short):
- [ ] Pick expression evaluator (WASM vs closed expression set)
- [ ] Proto for compact contract storage (2KB limit)
- [ ] Console UX sketch for viewing violations + toggles
- [ ] SDK helpers + examples for JS/Go/Python
- [ ] Run small internal cost experiment and lock remediation budget default

Notes to self:
- Keep enforcement off by default. Customers will want observe-only to start.
- Consider signing contracts with route version so we can track regressions after model upgrades.
- Ensure telemetry exposes which model variant produced failure so we can correlate model changes -> assertion drift.

End of scratchpad.
